detailed_rationale:
Sagility India is a healthcare-focused business process/technology-enabled services provider serving US healthcare payers and providers exclusively — a single-market concentration (100% US client base) but within a very large addressable market: the company itself cites roughly 1.2% share of the US healthcare outsourcing market as of 2023, implying a long runway if it can keep taking share. The company came public via IPO in late 2024, with PE sponsor EQT (through IGI Holding) the controlling shareholder pre-listing; promoter holding has fallen from 82.4% (Dec-2024) to 50.95% (Jun-2026), which reads as ordinary post-IPO/post-lockup sponsor monetization rather than a distress signal.

Growth has been genuinely strong and broad-based: TTM revenue growth of 29% and TTM profit growth of 54%, with operating margins stable around 24% and net margins around 13%. The quant quality score (8.6) looks low mainly because reported ROE (11% last year, 7.6% 3-year average) is depressed by heavy amortization of intangibles from the 2021 buyout/IPO corporate structure (depreciation rose from ₹147cr in FY22 to ₹487cr in FY26) — this is a real accounting drag on reported returns, not a reflection of weak underlying unit economics, and it should ease as the acquisition-related intangible base amortizes down over time. The single-client-geography concentration (US healthcare payers/providers only) is the genuine structural risk to monitor — any US healthcare-policy shock or major client loss would hit disproportionately given the lack of geographic diversification.
recommendation_rationale: Quant reads Hold, with the low quality score driven by an accounting (intangible-amortization) effect rather than weak operating economics; my research corroborates strong, broad-based growth and margins, tempered by real single-market client concentration risk. Hold is right — genuinely good growth at a reasonable multiple, but concentration risk and post-IPO sponsor overhang keep this from being a stronger call.
summary: Sagility India provides outsourced processing and technology services to US healthcare insurers and providers, and has grown revenue and profit strongly since its 2024 listing. Reported return ratios look modest mainly because of heavy non-cash amortization tied to the company's 2021 buyout structure, not because the underlying business is weak. The company's near-total reliance on the US healthcare market is the main risk to watch, but the growth and margin trends are genuinely encouraging.
positive_para: Strong, broad-based growth (revenue +29%, profit +54% TTM) with stable ~24% operating margins, a large addressable US healthcare outsourcing market where the company holds a small (~1.2%) share with room to keep taking share, and a reasonable 20.8x multiple for that growth rate.
negative_para: The business is entirely dependent on US healthcare payer/provider clients — any adverse US healthcare-policy shift or the loss of a major client would hit disproportionately hard given the lack of geographic or vertical diversification, and continued PE-sponsor stake reduction (down from 82% to 51% promoter holding since the IPO) remains a technical supply overhang to watch.
reverse_dcf_judgment: At roughly 20.8x trailing earnings for a business growing profit north of 50% (even allowing that some of the depressed prior-year base was itself amortization-driven), the multiple looks undemanding if growth and margins hold — cheap-to-fair, with the main risk being concentration in a single client geography rather than valuation.
